newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INE sees '97 Portugal investment up 5.0 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INE sees '97 Portugal investment up 5.0 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Investment in Portugal is expected to grow by at least five percent year-on-year in 1997, led by public companies, up from a 0.8-percent rise in 1996, the National Statistics Institute (INE) said.
"Public companies continue to show the greatest capacity to invest," a statement said. It projected public companies' investment would rise by 29.6 percent in 1997.

"As for private companies, growth is also expected to be positive (3.3 percent), but influenced by two major projects, the new bridge over the River Tagus and the Ford -Volkswagen plant in Palmela," it said.
Excluding the bridge and automotive investments, private companies' investment growth in Portugal is forecast to be at six percent year-on-year in 1997.
In 1996, private companies' investment fell by 1.9 percent. If the bridge and automotive investments are excluded, investment rose by 0.4 percent, INE said.
